title: The Haunting of Molly Hartley
full_review:
Though there's relatively little violence in first-time director Mickey Liddell's inept chiller, "The Haunting of Molly Hartley" (Freestyle), its twisted portrayal of evangelical Christianity and implicit denial of free will and divine providence make it entirely unsuitable for young viewers and demand careful interpretation by adults.

Joining the ranks of the crazy Christians seen all too often in this genre is born-again teen Alexis (Shanna Collins). Though shunned by her classmates at the upscale Huntington Academy as a "Bible thumper," she's given the task of welcoming newcomer Molly (Haley Bennett), who has just relocated to the area with her weak-willed father (Jake Weber).

They have good reason for wanting a fresh start, since Molly's seemingly normal mother (Marin Hinkle) had inexplicably tried to kill her and is now confined in an asylum. Molly's flashbacks show that her mother was motivated by fear of some terrible change associated with the girl's forthcoming 18th birthday.

Plagued by nosebleeds, panic attacks and murmuring voices in her head, Molly fears she too may be going insane. But she still manages to catch the eye of lacrosse jock Joseph (Chace Crawford) and win the friendship of hard-bitten party girl Leah (Shannon Marie Woodward), who acknowledges that Molly's problems are even worse than her own.

Long before its overwrought, philosophically skewed climax, which includes a baptism-turned-drowning attempt, this horror tale becomes tedious and completely unrewarding.

The film contains troubling thematic elements, underage drinking, one use of the F-word, occasional crude language and brief skimpy costuming. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
